title: O++ threshold count reported to Hamm (49) was a row count; unique-unit count is 42
notes: Self-caught error, not user-reported. While computing the O++ threshold sweep for the fig03 handout (restricting outputs/classification/grand_oplus_units.csv to area in {V4,TEO,FEF,PFC} and sweeping min_mean_correlation), I reported 'r>=0.67 -> n=49' and Hamm explicitly confirmed it ('for O++ the 49 is correct'). Re-verifying afterward (per this project's re-resolve-before-trusting doctrine) found the 49 was `((mean_correlation>=0.67) & (permutation_pval<=0.05)).sum()` on the RAW candidate table, which has one row per (unit, pattern_type) pair -- a unit qualifying under both 'O+' (strict peak-dominance-gated template) and 'O*+' (looser 2-of-9 template) pattern types appears as two separate rows. 7 of the 49 passing rows are such duplicate units. Deduplicating on (session_prefix, unit_row_idx) gives 42 unique units at r>=0.67, not 49 -- below Hamm's stated >=50 floor.

Re-swept the threshold on a deduplicated basis: r>=0.60 -> 79 units, r>=0.63 -> 66, r>=0.65 -> 52 (clears the >=50 floor), r>=0.66 -> 47, r>=0.67 -> 42. Corrected recommendation is min_mean_correlation=0.65 (52 unique units), not 0.67/49 as previously stated to Hamm.

This means Hamm's 'confirmed correct' applied to a number that was itself wrong -- surfaced immediately rather than letting the confirmed-but-incorrect number stand or silently swapping in the corrected one without flagging the discrepancy.
issues: Whatever script ultimately implements the O++ threshold (build_oplusplus_census.py / assign_o_plusplus_from_template_table in jnwb/unit_classification.py) needs to be checked for whether it already deduplicates on unit identity before counting/plotting -- if it does not, every panel B/E/F count downstream carries this same row-vs-unit inflation, not just my ad hoc threshold sweep. Not yet checked.

plan.falsifier: Closed when (1) the implementing script's counting logic is confirmed to dedupe on (session/session_prefix, unit_row/unit_row_idx) before reporting any n, and (2) Hamm re-confirms the corrected r=0.65/n=52 recommendation now that the counting bug is fixed -- not yet done.

verification.verdict: CONFIRMED as a real counting bug in my own ad hoc analysis (not yet checked in the actual pipeline scripts). The number Hamm confirmed as correct was wrong; corrected figure (r=0.65, n=52) needs fresh confirmation.
